title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
remaining_gap: Citation quality is established, but authorization-conditioned answerability is not the central construct.
verification_notes: ALCE is a benchmark for automatic evaluation of citation quality, correctness and fluency in retrieval-and-generation systems.

title: RAGAs: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
remaining_gap: Does not study authorization-conditioned evidence sufficiency or disclosure.
verification_notes: RAGAs is a reference-free RAG evaluation framework covering retrieval/context relevance, faithful use of context, and generation quality.

title: ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
remaining_gap: Does not center authorized-vs-unauthorized evidence or scope-conditioned abstention.
verification_notes: ARES evaluates context relevance, answer faithfulness and answer relevance and uses prediction-powered inference with human-annotated data.

title: Towards Fine-Grained Citation Evaluation in Generated Text
remaining_gap: Fine-grained citation support is studied without user authorization as an evidence condition.
verification_notes: The paper evaluates citation-support metrics across full, partial and no-support conditions and compares them with human judgements.

title: GaRAGe: A Benchmark with Grounding Annotations for RAG Evaluation
remaining_gap: Does not make authorization scope a first-class evidence variable.
verification_notes: GaRAGe contains 2366 questions and over 35K annotated retrieved passages and evaluates grounding and deflection when relevant grounding is absent.

title: MIRAGE: A Metric-Intensive Benchmark for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation
remaining_gap: Component-specific retrieval/generation robustness is studied without authorization-conditioned answerability.
verification_notes: MIRAGE contains 7,560 instances and evaluates retrieval/generation interactions with metrics for noise vulnerability, context acceptability, context insensitivity and context misinterpretation.

title: GroUSE: A Benchmark to Evaluate Evaluators in Grounded Question Answering
remaining_gap: Evaluator calibration/failure modes are the focus rather than authorization-conditioned RAG behavior.
verification_notes: GroUSE introduces 7 grounded-QA evaluator failure modes and 144 unit tests to assess automated grounded-answer evaluators.

title: RAGEval: Scenario Specific RAG Evaluation Dataset Generation Framework
remaining_gap: Scenario-specific benchmark generation does not center permission-conditioned evidence sufficiency.
verification_notes: RAGEval generates scenario-specific documents, questions, answers and references and evaluates completeness, hallucination and irrelevance.

title: Benchmarking LLM Faithfulness in RAG with Evolving Leaderboards
remaining_gap: Faithfulness benchmarking does not treat authorization scope as a distinct evidence universe.
verification_notes: The study benchmarks RAG faithfulness using HHEM and FaithJudge over summarization, QA and data-to-text tasks.

title: Investigating the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation at the Query Level
remaining_gap: Query perturbation robustness is extensively studied, but perturbation is not conditioned on authorization boundaries.
verification_notes: The paper studies sensitivity of RAG components to query perturbations and reports more than 1,092 experiments.

title: TableRAG: A Retrieval Augmented Generation Framework for Heterogeneous Document Reasoning
remaining_gap: Heterogeneous document reasoning is not the primary question.
verification_notes: TableRAG focuses on heterogeneous document reasoning including structured tables and reports strong results on public datasets and HeteQA.

title: MEMERAG: A Multilingual End-to-End Meta-Evaluation Benchmark for Retrieval Augmented Generation
remaining_gap: Multilingual meta-evaluation is distinct from authorization-conditioned evidence sufficiency.
verification_notes: MEMERAG evaluates multilingual RAG evaluators using native-language data and expert annotations of faithfulness and relevance.

title: Evaluation of Attribution Bias in Generator-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
remaining_gap: Attribution bias is not authorization-conditioned evidence sufficiency.
verification_notes: The study examines attribution sensitivity and authorship bias in generator-aware RAG.

title: RefusalBench: Generative Evaluation of Selective Refusal in Grounded Language Models
remaining_gap: Selective refusal is evaluated under flawed context, but user authorization is not the central experimental variable.
verification_notes: RefusalBench generates diagnostic test cases through 176 controlled perturbation strategies spanning six informational uncertainty categories and three intensity levels.

title: All Languages Matter: Understanding and Mitigating Language Bias in Multilingual RAG
remaining_gap: Cross-language evidence selection is not the proposed authority/sufficiency problem.
verification_notes: The paper studies language bias in multilingual RAG reranking and evidence selection across multiple languages.

title: When Good OCR Is Not Enough: Benchmarking OCR Robustness for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
remaining_gap: OCR-induced evidence degradation is distinct from authorization-conditioned evidence availability.
verification_notes: InduOCRBench evaluates downstream RAG robustness across 11 difficult document types and shows OCR quality does not guarantee downstream RAG quality.

title: StruNRAG: Evaluation of OCR-Induced Structural Noise on RAG Robustness
remaining_gap: Structural-noise perturbation is not permission-conditioned.
verification_notes: StruNRAG introduces bilingual QA data and controlled OCR structural perturbations including line insertion and paragraph/line interleaving.

title: Do LLMs Know When Evidence is Insufficient? An Evidence Sufficiency Benchmark for Answer-Abstention Calibration in RAG
remaining_gap: Evidence sufficiency is not conditioned on authorization scope.
verification_notes: The benchmark defines five evidence levels from full support through conflicting evidence and evaluates answer-abstention calibration.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective RAG
remaining_gap: Does not establish authorized evidence as a distinct answerability universe.
verification_notes: SURE-RAG evaluates support/refute/insufficient evidence with a set-level evidence sufficiency verifier and selective answering.

title: CiteGuard: Faithful Citation Attribution for LLMs via Retrieval-Augmented Validation
remaining_gap: Citation attribution does not address authorization-conditioned answerability.
verification_notes: CiteGuard reframes citation evaluation as attribution alignment and proposes a retrieval-aware citation validation framework.

title: CiteGuard-RAG: A Validation-Centered AI System for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering
remaining_gap: Validation-centered RAG is very close architecturally, but the reported study does not center authorized-only evidence sufficiency and unauthorized-only answer availability.
verification_notes: CiteGuard-RAG integrates hybrid retrieval, citation-constrained generation, sentence-level grounding validation, regeneration, refusal and controlled/external evaluation.

title: Authorization-First Retrieval: Enforcing Least Privilege in Multi-Agent RAG Systems
remaining_gap: Authorization-before-retrieval is directly studied, but the interaction with evidence sufficiency and abstention remains outside its core construct.
verification_notes: Authorization-First Retrieval formalizes authorization-before-retrieval and evaluates unauthorized context and answer leakage under controlled role/domain queries.

title: Permission-Aware RAG: Identity and Access Management-Based Access Filtering in Multi-Resource Environments
remaining_gap: Permission-aware retrieval is established, but evidence sufficiency and refusal under authorized/unauthorized evidence mixtures are not the primary construct.
verification_notes: IEEE Access paper proposes IAM-based access filtering for multi-resource RAG and addresses fine-grained enterprise access control.

title: Privacy-provisioned-permission-aware RAG in cloud using identity and access management, trust and large-language models
remaining_gap: Adds privacy-preserving IAM and trust mechanisms but does not center authorized-evidence sufficiency and abstention behavior.
verification_notes: Scientific Reports 2026 article describes permission-aware RAG with IAM, trust and encrypted embeddings; authorized candidates are gated before similarity ranking.

title: Securing the Agent: Vendor-Neutral, Multitenant Enterprise Retrieval and Tool Use
remaining_gap: Multitenant authorization and leakage are central, but evidence sufficiency/abstention under unauthorized-only evidence is not the core evaluation construct.
verification_notes: The paper presents a layered multitenant isolation architecture with policy-aware ingestion and retrieval-time gating and reports empirical leakage evaluation.

title: When Failures Propagate: Causal Failure Attribution in Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
remaining_gap: Studies interventional failure attribution in agentic multi-hop RAG, not authorization-conditioned evidence sufficiency.
verification_notes: AgenticRAG-FP injects certified faults at specified hops and evaluates whether post-hoc traces identify the injected failure location.

title: Counterfactual Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
remaining_gap: Counterfactual evidence conflict is studied without the authorized-vs-unauthorized evidence boundary.
verification_notes: Counterfactual RAG studies causally decisive evidence, counterfactual queries and conflicting evidence arbitration.

title: Efficiency vs. Verifiability in Evidence-Aware RAG
remaining_gap: Studies compression-induced grounding loss rather than access-conditioned evidence sufficiency.
verification_notes: The paper evaluates how prompt compression affects answer correctness and citation grounding under controlled compression levels.
